answers.text: The most common form of hyperthyroidism is an autoimmune disorder called Grave’s disease.
In Grave’s disease, the immunoglobulins of the immune system mimic thyroid stimulating hormone, which is the messenger hormone that signals the release of Thyroxine (T4)

In hyperthyroidism, the excess thyroid hormone increases the sensitivity to adrenaline, speeding up the heart and increasing heart rate and contractility. Therefore, Beta blockers such as propranolol or other OLOL drugs are used in addition to other drugs to decrease the heart rate back to normal.

params.textField: This activity includes medications that treat hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism. For hyperthyroidism, the medication that is used to slow down the heart rate and decrease contractility includes *atenolol* and other beta blockers. It does not treat the hyperthyroidism but only the racing heart. One of the medications that can be used to decrease the formation of the thyroid hormones in hyperthyroidism is *carbimazole*, but it is a pregnancy category D drug. *iodine 131* may need to be given in cases of hyperthyroidism to destroy some of the cells in the thyroid. Unfortunately, this may lead to hypothyroidism. The gold standard therapy for hypothyroidism is *levothyroixine* which is a synthetic form of T4 that is administered orally or intravenously and is a pregnancy category A drug. If the person also has liver disease, and is unable to convert the T4 into the more active T3, they will be given *liothyronine* which is a synthetic form of T3. Since thyroid hormones themselves and synthetic replacement drugs have a very long half life of over one week, care is taken to gradually increase the levels of thyroid hormone to the ideal level, and this may take months of treatment.
